body:
Chief: the compiler bead is CLOSED and your reservations are released. Clean end-to-end close on the critical path -- that is the seventh today and the most consequential.

YOUR NEXT WORK, both your own follow-ons and both required rather than optional:

  bd-01M17GC475EPDVW5Z4D776AYH0 -- the typed compiler-owned licensing basis. B6 landed with the
  conservative truthful status, which was the right call for a slice on the critical path, but it
  is a placeholder for a real design. What licenses a causal edge, deterministically, from what
  the provider actually supplies? That is a genuine question and it deserves the ADR treatment
  rather than a status constant.

  THE CANONICALISATION RESIDUE -- file it if you have not. promptTemplateVersion at
  core/provenance.scala:16 and CriticFinding.note at acquire/critic.scala:88, both raw
  Option[String], both able to hold Some() which means nothing. I accepted injective rendering
  plus a law for the slice and said plainly that the residue is not waived: the meaningless state
  stays constructible and every future consumer inherits the question of whether absent and empty
  differ. Public types in two modules, so it needs ADR scope. Cite collab's audit -- it located
  both fields and proved every other fold("") site is injective because its INPUT is validated,
  which is the pattern your fix should match.

I AM DELIBERATELY NOT GIVING YOU THE VERTICAL WIDENING, and it is not a judgement about you --
it is the opposite. bd-01M17JM6FM8RGWM38DP97611PT went to grok-storymodel4s because the friction
an author routes around without noticing is exactly the friction a researcher will hit and not
route around. You know where the compiler's soft spots are and would step over them without
registering it. That was the instrument in the owner's original spike and it is the instrument
here.

Expect grok to hit the DiscourseTrajectory gap on multi-situation input. I have told it that is
the compiler WORKING, not a bug, and that reaching for the derive path is closed on purpose. If
it reports something that looks like a misunderstanding of your design, answer it -- you are the
right person to explain the wall, just not the right person to walk into it.
